name: USDD
oneLiner: USDD is the Tron DAO Reserve's CDP-and-PSM stablecoin, designed as overcollateralized but historically traded below peg through multiple stress episodes.
collateral: Current reserves are split across Smart Allocator stablecoin deployments, TRX and sTRX CDP vault collateral, and USDT held in PSM/direct vaults; Bitcoin was removed from reserves in August 2024
pegMechanism: CDP model with minimum 130% collateral ratio; Peg Stability Module enables 1:1 minting/redemption against USDT and USDC

oracleRisk.summary: TRON DAO says Chainlink Data Feeds are the official oracle solution securing TRON DeFi including the USDD protocol, with no stronger USDD-specific failover documented.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: USDD is tracked on Tron, Ethereum, and BSC, while the workflow evidence resolves Across-style cross-chain route signals rather than issuer-native bridge controls. The reviewed profile treats cross-chain movement as a liquidity/intent route.

applicabilityBasis.summary: USDD is presented as the TRON DAO Reserve's dollar-pegged stablecoin for payments, with over-collateralized reserves and PSM swap/redemption mechanics.

genius.notes: USDD has self-reported reserve and PSM/redemption disclosures (usdd.io/data), but no formal third-party attestation. No GENIUS PPSI approval, application, or comparability determination for a foreign issuer exception was found. TRON DAO Reserve is Dominica-domiciled; Treasury has not yet finalized criteria for "comparable foreign regulation" under GENIUS. The April 2026 OFAC-coordinated Tether USDT freeze on TRON wallets and May 2026 UK sanctions on HTX are not GENIUS Act enforcement actions against USDD or its issuer.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: No GENIUS PPSI approval, official application, state-qualified approval, or registered/comparability-determined foreign-issuer exception was found for USDD or its issuer TRON DAO Reserve. No Treasury determination of comparable foreign regulation has been made for any jurisdiction as of this review date. The GENIUS Act approval framework itself remains in proposed-rulemaking phase.

blacklistabilityReview.sourceFreeRationale: Freeze-only re-review: USDD has no confirmed direct holder-balance freeze in reviewed metadata, but resolves to Upstream through stablecoin reserve and DeFi exposure.
blacklistabilityReview.evidence: USDD resolves to Upstream through USDT/USDC PSM and stablecoin DeFi exposure rather than direct token freeze authority.

mintAuthority.summary: USDD mints through Maker-style collateralized TRON DAO Reserve rails; Ethereum token source exposes warded mint authority and the USDD Join contract is the resolved direct minter, while governance/Pause/Vat administration remains unresolved.

controls.label: USDD Tron Join (active ward / direct minter)
controls.evidence: At Tron block 83506136 (2026-06-11): wards(TronJoin) on USDD token (TXDk8mbtRbXeYuMNS83CfKPaYYT8XWv9Hz) = 1 (confirmed ward). Tron Vat (TH5dhX7o39afSbfDT2e3c9k4itWjNKD4D9) live() = 1 (active). All other queried addresses (Pause, PauseProxy, GovActionsProxy) have ward=0 on the token. The legacy ETH-side 1.0 Vat/Join queried in the June 2026 review was caged, but USDD 2.0 documentation later introduced an Ethereum PSM mint/redeem route; Pharos no longer treats Ethereum as permanently disabled.

controls.label: USDD Tron GovActionsProxy (governance executor)
controls.evidence: Tron Pause (TNq6E9XsQfrzqVwam67LApZQx1omsj8dyW) authority() = GovActionsProxy (TXzhj9Xh8xfzerjinRyM5TfoBL7Cw5hk5d); Pause delay() = 0 (no timelock). GovActionsProxy.authority() = zero address (no higher authority set); GovActionsProxy govActions() = TDLgCe2SatVew6PxSwYmqsc3zfahqXwuqX and pause() = Pause contract. This contract's cast() function is the system's governance executor. The signer set that can call cast() was not confirmed — authority()=zero means access control falls back to contract-level access checks or is operated by the deployer.

controls.label: USDD Tron GovActionsProxy owner — single-key account (governance executor)
controls.evidence: GovActionsProxy.owner() returned 41b28033...eb069 (TSF2rqLdrrZG7PZkDxtvu6B2PTpofidMAX) via triggerconstantcontract; trongrid getaccount shows a normal account with 1-of-1 owner and active permissions (single keypair, no Tron-native multisig). All recent GovActionsProxy transactions originate from this account; with authority()=zero, ds-auth restricts cast() to this owner.

review.evidence: At ETH block 25294783 and Tron block 83506136 (2026-06-11), the legacy ETH Vat/Join was caged while Tron Join remained an active ward. USDD 2.0 documentation later introduced an Ethereum PSM route for native USDD mint/redeem, so the profile no longer states that active minting is Tron-only. Tron governance remains concentrated: Pause delay=0, GovActionsProxy owner resolved to a single-key Tron account, and this owner is the sole historical governance caller.

reserveReview.rationale: USDD reports Smart Allocator positions as a protocol aggregate while separately identifying direct USDT PSM exposure.
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: Stablecoin positions inside Smart Allocator cannot be assigned individual dependency weights.

nonLinkDispositions.rationale: The allocator bucket aggregates multiple positions and does not expose stablecoin-level percentages.

notices.title: Historical reserve-governance and depeg risk
notices.message: USDD has a history of peg stress, including a March 2023 depeg around $0.93. In August 2024, Tron DAO Reserve removed roughly 12,000 BTC from USDD collateral without prior DAO approval, leaving reserve governance dependent on Tron DAO Reserve decisions.
